item.title: NFL Icon Mike Ditka passes away at 86
item.description: The Chicago Bears and the NFL lost a true legend of the sport today with the passing of Mike Ditka at 86.
item.content:encoded:
The Chicago Bears and the NFL lost a true legend of the sport today, as Mike Ditka passed away at 86.

Born Michael Keller Dyczko Jr. on October 18, 1939, in Carnegie, Pennsylvania, his family changed their name to Dikta because Dyczko was too difficult for people to pronounce. He went on to become one of the most recognizable figures not only in sports but also in pop culture.

Ditka won a championship as a player with the Bears in 1963, and he led them to the franchise’s only Super Bowl win in 1985. As a player, he revolutionized the tight end position by winning Rookie of the Year in 1961 and becoming the first tight end to surpass 1,000 yards in a season. He was also the first tight end inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in the class of 1988.

As a coach, he was the perfect hire for a franchise that needed a spark, and his fiery passion came through in everything he did. He led the Bears to the playoffs seven times over his 11 seasons in the Windy City and to three NFC Championship Games.

Jarrett Payton, whose father, Walter Payton, was the centerpiece of Ditka’s offense during their run to Super Bowl XX, made the announcement live on air after receiving the news.

Jarrett also shared a statement from the family:

It is with profound sadness that we announce the passing of our beloved husband, father, grandfather, and friend, Mike Ditka. While the world knew Mike as a Hall of Fame football player, legendary coach, and leader of the Chicago Bears’ Super Bowl XX championship team, we knew him as the heart of our family. Mike will be missed beyond measure and remembered forever.

With love and gratitude, The Ditka Family

item.title: Eagles News: It’s Willie Lampkin time
item.description: Philadelphia Eagles news and links for 10/9/26.
item.content:encoded:
Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation!

Really excited to see how Willie Lampkin fares in his first NFL start. Despite his unconventional frame, he might be a pretty good player? Lampkin was the 11th-highest graded interior offensive lineman by Pro Football Focus during the 2025 preseason. He was sixth-highest in the 2026 preseason. Lampkin stood out in a good way during training camp practices and he drew unprompted praise from Lane Johnson in a conversation the former Eagles right tackle had with some reporters off to the side with no microphones or cameras after a joint training camp practice with the Patriots. Let’s see what he’s got!

Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links …

Willie Lampkin to make NFL history Sunday in first career start – NBCSP

There’s never been an NFL offensive lineman built like Willie Lampkin. There’s about to be. Lampkin stands 5-foot-11, 290 pounds. And when he made his NFL debut playing four special teams snaps in the Eagles’ opener vs. the Commanders, he became the heaviest offensive lineman in NFL history under six feet. That’s a distinction previously held by Terry Long, who was 5-11, 272, and played in 105 games for the Steelers from 1984 through 1991. Now, for at least one week, Lampkin will be a starter. With Landon Dickerson not eligible to come off Injured Reserve until next week and Cam Jurgens now a Baltimore Raven, Lampkin will play regular-season offensive line snaps for the first time in his career. It may be at guard and it may be at center. Lampkin and Drew Kendall are both natural centers who got reps at guard this summer, but one of them will have to start at left guard. Most likely it will be Lampkin because you would think they wouldn’t want to move a 24-year-old Kendall to guard when he’s just starting to play well at center. Although it’s easier to hide a 5-11 guy at center than guard. So we’ll see. Either way, Lampkin on Sunday will become the Eagles’ shortest offensive line starter in 69 years, since 5-11 Abe Gibron started 12 games at left guard in 1957.

There’s almost a foot between Markel Bell and Willie Lampkin. But they’ve become ‘brothers’ as O-Line careers take off. – Inquirer

When the two players first met, over the summer, they realized they shared a resilient spirit. Before long, they were inseparable; “always together” at the practice facility and at the stadium, in Lampkin’s telling. “He’s like my brother, man,” the guard said of Bell. “He’s like a humble beast.” Like any brothers would, they began to engage in some good-natured ribbing, mostly about the ACC rivalry between UNC and Miami. They never faced each other, but Lampkin will never let Bell forget about the Tar Heels’ 41-31 win over the Hurricanes in October of 2023. “I always tell him that we beat them,” Lampkin said. “I got my dub over Miami.” He also gave Bell a nickname (which appears to have been borrowed from reality TV personality Alexis Radcliff). “I call him ‘Big ‘Kel not the Little One,’” Lampkin said. “He hates when I say that. I’ve heard it online and I always just say it to him. I don’t even know, I just heard it. I always be like, ‘Big ‘Kel not the Little One.’” Added Bell: “He just be trollin’, he just be trollin’. I laugh and I tell him to get out of my face.”

Eagles-Jaguars Game Preview: 5 questions and answers with the Week 5 enemy – BGN

1 – The Jags are 16-5 in the Liam Coen era. What’s he done to turn this team around since Super Bowl LII champion Doug Pederson was fired? … When Coen was hired, the thought in Jacksonville was, “He seems to have the goods as a playcaller. But can he also be a culture-setter?” 18 months later, the answer is a resounding yes. Look no further than Jacksonville’s latest victory: a gritty five-point win in Cincinnati. The Bengals may not be juggernauts, but the last time the Jaguars played at their stadium (Week 2 last season), Jake Browning led a stunning second-half comeback to steal the dub. “Winning ain’t easy in this league,” Coen told the locker room after getting redemption this past week. “Do we have to clean sht up? Absolutely. But guess what? Our culture prevailed. Our fcking toughness prevailed … The last time we were in this locker room, in a similar type situation, it wasn’t a great feeling, right? Talk about growth. Talk about us as a unit, us as an organization, what the f*ck we’re building. That’s what I’m proud of.”

Jaguars vs. Eagles: Matchup History Through the Decades – Big Cat Country

The Jacksonville Jaguars begin their London stretch this week against the Philadelphia Eagles. The two teams have played each other eight times, and the Eagles currently lead the series 5-3. The Jags are technically the home team this week, so let’s look at Philadelphia being defeated in Jacksonville throughout the decades.

Eagles-Jaguars preview: 5 things to watch – PhillyVoice

If there’s a weakness on this Jaguars team, it’s probably their offensive line. It’s just kind of an average group. But, they’re (mostly) healthy, so at least there’s that. The only injury they have is to starting RG Patrick Mekari, who has been on injured reserve all season so far. The Eagles’ defensive line has been disappointing this season. One way the Eagles can win this game is if the pass rush makes a few big plays and creates turnovers. I just don’t see it. My guess? The Jags run a conservative offense on Sunday, take what the Eagles give them, and let their talented defense shut down the Eagles’ woeful offense.

NFL Week 5 preview: Picks, predictions, schedule, betting odds, fantasy tips – ESPN

Bold prediction: The Jaguars will win by two touchdowns. Philadelphia is 2-2 and ranks 27th in EPA per play on offense and 25th on defense. That is rough. And in three of those games, the Eagles had the now-retired Johnson, too. We can and should think about these teams dramatically differently now than when the season began (for the Jaguars, this is a good thing!). […] Why you should watch this game: You can play a game called “how many Eagles players do I recognize?” as they take the field without Johnson (retired), TE Dallas Goedert (knee), WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and RB Saquon Barkley (hamstring) — and now Jurgens is a Raven! If Willie Lampkin gets the start on the now sparse offensive line, as expected, he’ll be the shortest Eagles offensive lineman (5-foot-11) to start in over 60 years.

Eagles trading Cam Jurgens fully accelerates a mid-season rebuild on the offensive line | Five Thoughts – PHLY Eagles

Final thought, written a few hours removed from all the commotion of the day: The Eagles find themselves fully in a transition on the offensive line now. They’ve made bets, at least in the short-term, that some combination of Lampkin, Kendall, and Bell can be part of a rebuilt group tasked with replacing one of the best collections of offensive-line talent the NFL has seen in recent memory. And they’ve made that bet having just split with one of the league’s best talent developers at the position in Jeff Stoutland. It’s fair to ask whether Roseman has done enough replenishing the offensive line for this sudden rebuild given the shaky ground Johnson, Dickerson, and Jurgens were on even entering this year’s training camp. As I said on our show Tuesday before the Jurgens trade, it’s hard to argue with any individual pick Roseman has made in each of the last few drafts, but the cumulative affect of missing out on the offensive line prospects at the latter stages of the first and second rounds over the years has now shown up. The best argument by my estimation would be in favor of taking former Arizona State tackle prospect Max Iheanachor last April instead of Makai Lemon (something I suggested in our shadow draft episode in the spring). Outside of that, an aggressive trade up the draft board may have been the only revisionist history suggestion worth levying toward Roseman. If the trio of Kendall, Lampkin, and Bell are up to the challenge, the Eagles will find themselves in a similar situation picking late in the first round again in 2027. If they’re not, though, that issue may “solve” itself …

The Best Bets of NFL Week 5 – The Ringer

The Eagles offensive line went from elite to average to bad in the last three years. They’re trying to implement a new offense, but they still aren’t able to consistently throw over the middle, generate yards after the catch, or run play-action. There’s a reason I’ve bet against the Eagles heavily each of the last three weeks, but I think the market is now properly pricing them here. Edges don’t last forever in sports betting, and the time to bet against Philly in the season-long and game-to-game markets has come and probably gone now. This is the stingiest run defense they’ve faced all year, and Will Shipley is the starting RB behind two brand new interior offensive linemen. I’ll have more Jags thoughts in the weeks to come, but I’m continuing to notice that their defense is top three in points per drive allowed since Anthony Campanile became defensive coordinator to start 2025. Consider Jaguars alternate spreads.

    Eagles in London: Inside their travel plans and Jemal Singleton’s homecoming – The Athletic

    “The whole travel part, I think it’s tricky because of the lack of a bye week after, like you kind of got to stay on some sort of a schedule,” said kicker Jake Elliott, the Eagles’ longest-tenured player. “I understand the science behind it all, and I think we’re doing a good happy medium of adjusting our week this week to kind of adjust domestically.” Elliott called it a “two-week plan” focused on both this weekend’s game and next week’s. And the players “don’t want to get too far to the other side and then have to readjust back next week.” The organization also believes it benefits players to rehab and recover at their own facility this week rather than in a hotel abroad. The players slept in their own beds during the week. When they fly late Friday, the emphasis is on getting a good night’s sleep on the plane, on a schedule comparable to the one they maintained in Philadelphia. Their travel accommodations, with with lie-flat seats and minimal time commuting to and from the airport and waiting in security lines and at the gate, are better than those of the legions of Eagles fans (and the group of Eagles reporters) making the flight. The overseas trip has not even been a major topic this week. Perhaps in different circumstances, the travel might be more scrutinized. But a future Hall of Famer retired, a two-time Pro Bowler was traded and the Eagles are preparing for Sunday’s game without key starters. They have bigger concerns than an unconventional travel schedule. “I honestly have no opinion on it,” Jalen Hurts said. “My approach is just to prepare. Doesn’t really matter where we play.”

    NFL Week 5 bold predictions: Jahmyr Gibbs breaks Barry Sanders’ record; ‘Hawks punish Brock Purdy – NFL.com

    Jalen Hurts’ only TD pass in London game goes to Travis Hunter. An Eagles squad in crisis will find no respite against the Jaguars’ second-ranked defense in points allowed. Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith are ailing with hamstring injuries, and the team’s anchor at right tackle, Lane Johnson, retired on Tuesday. It’s not a good equation with Philly heading off to Europe to face a stingy, opportunistic defense that’s already tallied eight takeaways. Travis Hunter accounted for one of those with his first career interception in Week 3, and he brought down another pick in Week 4 that was wiped out by a roughing the passer penalty. His next INT comes Sunday — this one stands, and he takes it to the house. Better yet, he’s the only player on either team to score a touchdown off a Jalen Hurts pass.

    Spadaro: Jalen Hurts and the Eagles’ offense embrace ‘next-man-up’ mentality – PhiladelphiaEagles.com

    POV for quarterback Jalen Hurts Sunday in London against Jacksonville? A new left guard. A second start for a rookie at right tackle. New personnel at running back. Young talent at wide receiver. The tight end position not looking as expected when Training Camp began. So, what is he supposed to do? Go with it. Roll with it. Work hard during this week of practice and head into the game against Jacksonville with confidence and trust. That’s how the NFL works. That’s just how it has to be. “I feel good about it. I feel good about the guys that we have. I feel good about the work that we’re putting forward and the week will tell how much that will improve,” Hurts said on Wednesday at his weekly press conference at the Jefferson Health Training Complex. “I get ready for meetings. We’ve got a lot of opportunity in front of us. We’ve got a lot of room to improve and we’re attacking that every day.”

    Roundtable Reactions: Ravens trade for Cam Jurgens – Baltimore Beatdown

    The Ravens moving a future second-rounder definitely raises an eyebrow with a front office that has been traditionally stingy about keeping their draft picks. I’ve seen the word “desperate” floating around, and I don’t necessarily think it’s the wrong word to use for this situation, but maybe just a reminder that a move made in desperation doesn’t mean it was a panic move. The Ravens were very depleted along the O-line at this early stage of the season and now once again face the specter of Lamar Jackson missing time with an injury. To keep the season on its trajectory, they had to make a move to solidify the trenches, so they paid a premium price for Cam Jurgens. Jurgens has struggled playing out of position for Philly, but moving back to Center could be the thing he needs to have the best parts of his game restored (we hope). History has shown it’s bad business to deal with Howie Roseman, but then again, Baltimore got something for nothing from Philly in the Jaire Alexander move, so who knows how this one shakes out. I’m glad they have another O-lineman in the room that’s not just a body, but a guy who has shown a high level of competence. — Kevin McNeils.

    NY Giants get WR Malik Nabers, OT Andrew Thomas back at practice – Big Blue View

    The New York Giants got some good news on the injury front Thursday as they continued to prepare for a Week 5 game against the Washington Commanders. Wide receiver Malik Nabers, who said he was “sore” on Wednesday and did not practice, was a limited practice participant. He continues to manage his knee in his return from a torn ACL. Left tackle Andrew Thomas, managing a groin injury, returned to practice as a limited participant after not practicing on Wednesday. Running back Cam Skattebo was again a limited participant, but shed the red, non-contact jersey on Thursday.

    The Cowboys’ brand is soul-crushing embarrassment – SB Nation

    The Cowboys were awful on Thursday night, and managed to make history in the worst possible way. By losing to the Buccaneers, Dallas became the second team since 1975 to lose to an 0-4 team at home. It’s what we’ve come to expect from the Cowboys’ exceptionalism over the last three decades — because exceptionally mediocre has become their brand. It would be easier to swallow for fans if there was a singular nexus of blame, something you can easily point to and say, “This is why Dallas is losing.“ Unfortunately, there’s no one answer to what’s gone wrong, no silver bullet, nothing to focus on, correct, and get better. Sure, you can point to Jerry and Stephen Jones as being the problem — and make no mistake, they are problems, but there are so many issues. Dallas has shuffled coaches over the years, made splashy trades, invested huge money in their stars, and yet they’ll still lose to a winless football team with a backup QB under center making his first NFL start.

    Cowboys vs. Buccaneers: 2 winners and 3 losers – Blogging The Boys

    Loser: Dak Prescott. Dak Prescott looked nothing like the quarterback who engineered last week’s comeback. Prescott went 24-of-42 for 316 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions. Several throws were simply inaccurate, but his response to pressure was the bigger concern. Tampa Bay sped up his internal clock and too often made Prescott hurry even before the rush actually reached him. Some responsibility belongs to the protection and the play calling, but Prescott is the veteran quarterback being trusted to identify pressure and find the correct answer. Against a defense that entered the night with only six sacks in four games, Dallas shouldn’t have looked this uncomfortable. Tampa Bay dictated the terms, and Prescott struggled to change them.

    Commanders roster moves: Sixth-round NFL draft pick Kaytron Allen waived – Hogs Haven

    Allen was expected to make an immediate impact and looked good during the summer and was thought to have an active role in the rushing game, though that outlook has changed with the personnel available. The running back room was getting crowded and Allen was an odd man out, though the Commanders will probably try to sign him to the practice squad, but there’s no guarantee that he’ll clear waivers. Seattle signed Robert Henry Jr. off the practice squad, where Craig Reynolds still resides. It’s hard to imagine the Commanders giving up on Allen, even as a lower-round draft pick. Time will tell if he’s able to get to the practice squad. All it takes is one team that liked him in the draft to sign him to their active roster.

    Patriots promote safety Mike Brown to 53-man roster after consecutive elevations – Pats Pulpit

    The Patriots re-signed outside linebacker Jose Ramirez to the 17-man practice squad after he cleared waivers the afternoon prior. Ramirez, 27, first agreed to terms in Foxborough as the calendar turned to September. A promotion from the practice squad to the 53-man roster followed for the 6-foot-2, 252-pound edge rusher as safety Dell Pettus landed on injured reserve last month. From there, Ramirez appeared in two road matchups. He recorded one solo tackle across 30 snaps between defense and special teams before being waived. Entering the NFL in the sixth round of the 2023 draft at No. 196 overall, Ramirez checked into four games while a member of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and notched one quarterback hit. The former MAC Defensive Player of the Year by way of Arizona, Riverside City College and Eastern Michigan spent last year with the CFL’s Hamilton Tiger-Cats en route to reaching a futures contract with the Philadelphia Eagles in January.

item.title: Carolina Panthers 2026 fan mailbag: Bye week, injury returns, food stuff, Brenton Bersin life coach, and more!
item.description: Answering all your questions in this week’s fan mailbag!
item.content:encoded:
Hello CSR! Welcome to Brian Answers, part two of your weekly Panthers fan mailbag for everyone! We’re at the bye week, players are healing up, and you have questions. Let’s dive right in!

Walker Clement: How much of Bryce Young’s resurgence (surgence?) is attributable to unpublished and probably spurious reports of him hiring Brenton Bersin as his life coach?

I would say about 50%. I’m sure Nick Scott being there to mentor him as the uncrowned captain of the defense also helps. Both Brenton and Nick know all about excelling despite catching the vitriol of the fan base. So this era of Sunshine in Carolina can definitely be attributed to the devoted disciples of House Bersin.

TXPanther: Is this the worst hypothetical trade scenario you’ve ever seen? It’s at least top 5.

Yes. This is a reminder that fans of NFL teams can be very dumb. I would imagine a lot of non-Panthers fans don’t realize the Panthers just gave Jalen Coker a nice extension. A sick trade for an EDGE might get made, but Jalen Coker will not be a part of it.

Brice Guild: I am starting to see posts here and have seen talking heads from many national sports shows say, ” Bryce Youngs has increased his arm strength this year” .

What say you? Is that really a thing? Or could it be he is confident and more assertive with his throwing motion, or a better pocket to step up into or has BY actually increased his actual power and speed of his passes? ?

I’m sure Bryce Young has gotten objectively stronger since being drafted as part of an NFL training program. But I do think the zip and accuracy on his passes comes more from being more confident in the system and mechanically cleaning some things up. He’s still making some pretty crazy throws without having his mechanics in proper structure, so I attribute most of the change to just being decisive and trusting his reads. He’s been making a lot of checks at the line presnap as well so he’s clearly settled in to the snap to snap flow that a good quarterback in the league has to.

schrodingersblackcat: Say the stars align. Bryce emerges as a consistent QB1 this season with a few more flashes of Drew Brees 2.0, injuries don’t derail us any further, our offense becomes a major NFL storyline with Tet and Coker becoming household names. Maybe we even somehow end up winning a playoff game. What does Brad Idzik’s future look like?

Its an interesting situation, Brad Idzik is basically a direct extension of Dave Canales but if the offensive production continues as it has, I would imagine he’s interviewing at least for head coaching positions this off-season and likely gone following the 2027 season to a head coaching job. The NFL head coaching group is constantly churning and many organizations like to pair an offensive leaning head coach with a shiny young quarterback. I would love for him to stick around for as long as possible if the offense and Bryce Young continues on this pace, but I do believe Dave Canales is already developing his successor. Remember, Dave has made a point to give some of his positional coaches reps to call plays in the preseason, that is definitely by design for long term development.

DannyLimes: given the state of our injuries, the bucs falling apart and the saints wild inconsistency… are the falcons suddenly favourites for the NFC behind a currently health Mike Penix and Bijan Robinson?

I could definitely see the Falcons being a head of the Panthers at some point in the season, their defense has been very good minus the Panthers week 2 game, which mostly was a blowout because of the Falcons offense and a 3rd string QB. The NFC South playoff picture will likely be messy once again this season. The Bucs just won last night and that puts them only a game or two outside of the top of the division right now.

JakeNCVA: We are four games into the season. There are three undefeated teams, eight at 3-1, twelve at 2-2, four at 1-3, and five at 0-4 — so only 11 of 32 have winning records (I know its early!). The only team I have not seen play are the 49’ers — but everyone else looks beatable — including the 4-0 Minnesota Vikings. The Panthers remaining schedule all of the sudden looks easier than it did a few weeks ago — both because of how the rest of the league is playing and how well the Panthers are playing – even with 2 losses they look to be trending way up from the past.

What is your revised look at the W-L record? We only have Minn, Baltimore and Seattle left that are above 500 – at the moment. Do you think the teams have settled into their “personalities” for the season yet, or are they still working things out, and we may still see hot risers and plummeting disappointments.

I’m still sitting at around 9-10 wins. I expect the Panthers offense to come down to Earth against some of the better defenses on the schedule and the injury bug has already hit them very hard. Don’t get me wrong, 12 wins wouldn’t necessarily surprise me, but I expect the Panthers to be in more close games than blow outs, so the margin for error is much smaller there.

TXPanther: Since you miss food questions, what are your:

Favorite dessert orders at The Cheesecake Factory?

Top 3 fast food spots and favorite order at each one?

I’ve only eaten at Cheesecake Factory maybe twice in my life, so I’ll leave that one up for debate in the comments.

Top fast food spots are fun! In no particular order

  • Wawa: Honey Smoked Turkey hoagie with all the usual sub fixin’s and spicy mustard. Or the Gobbler Bowl around Thanksgiving time.
  • Popeye’s: Spicy Chicken Sandwich
  • White Castle: Crave Case, easily. The restaurants are spread thin but I’ve found a way to them many times on a long road trip.

SmoothC: If panthers made 1 trade for a decent to good player, but only 1, would you get a pass rusher, CB or OL?

I’d probably go with a cornerback. EDGE rushers are always expensive to trade for and I think the Panthers have enough talent on the shelf that should be returning on the offensive line. They will likely just try to weather that storm, but it seems they’ll have some reinforcements coming after the bye.

WanderingJanusz: Which game(s) are you watching this Sunday and why

Chargers vs Broncos because I apparently hate myself and loaded up on Chargers in Dynasty fantasy with Justin Herbert (traded Javonte Williams for him, L) and I drafted Omarion Hampton 2nd overall in the rookie draft last year, and I drafted RJ Harvey in the first round of that same draft. So watching just to hate my dynasty squad. And I’ll probably have the Jets/Browns game on because I ALSO drafted Quinshon Judkins in the first round of that same rookie draft. Fantasy has not been kind to me this year. Don’t play dynasty.

KSUDD: You missed food questions, so top three cuisines? For me it’s Mexican, Japanese, and Greek in that order.

I would say Mediterranean Fish dishes, Japanese, and southern BBQ. I always enjoy the catch of the day when I am travelling overseas, sushi is one of my favorite things, and you just can’t beat some good old BBQ from the south. Green beans and bacon are my go-to side.

Bull123: All I’m really interested in asking for are injury updates

Lewis, Coker, Freeling, Phillips at top of list

Updates on brooks and XL as well…I guess

The last update we got on Damien Lewis is he would “miss a few weeks”. So I would assume he’s not going to be available for week 6. The Panthers are “hopeful” Jalen Coker will be available following the bye week. Canales also said that the injuries to both Monroe Freeling and Jaelan Phillips aren’t believed to be serious and they could suit up for week 6.

Jonathon Brooks was placed on IR so he is eligible to return around week 9/10, if he’s good to go following surgery. Xavier Legette could be back within the next 3 weeks.

That’s all for this week, Panthers fans! Join us next week for another edition of the mailbag!

item.title: Bengals News: Should Cincinnati claim Kaytron Allen
item.description: An unexpected opportunity to add depth.
item.content:encoded:
One underrated area of need that the Cincinnati Bengals are getting a bit exposed on is depth at the running back position. Chase Brown and Samaje Perine or good at what they do, but what the team really needs is a running back who can go out there and get that tough yard or two when needed.

It just so happens that one has been made available by the Washington Commanders:

The Washington Commanders shockingly cut rookie running back Kaytron Allen, a sixth-round pick, while juggling the roster around to fit players returning from injury. That move exposes Allen to waivers, where the Bengals would be wise to have an interest.

Right now defenses aren’t really respecting the running game in those short yardage situations, and Cincinnati hasn’t given them reason to need to. However, even just having the threat of being able to do that can open up more possibilities for Joe Burrow and the offense while also taking pressure off the passing game. It is a fairly low risk move that they should consider.

Bengals News

Quick Hits | Bengals Working Through Injuries; (Jordan) Battle Of Miami; The King And I

It looks like Jordan Battle will get another opportunity to start by default against Miami as Kyle Dugger has yet to even practice since getting hurt in Week 3. Bryan Cook was at least limited Thursday, so maybe he can make a return.

Bengals’ Jordan Battle reveals subtle Malik Willis tell ahead of Week 5 matchup against Dolphins

There are people who are saying this isn’t a big deal and others talking about how dumb it is. At this point, I would just love to see him make a tackle on 3rd-&-very long to get off the field rather than whiffing in the most comedic way possible. Battle would be a totally acceptable safety if he could just make these tackles that he has unfortunately made a habit of missing.

Ja’Marr Chase returns to practice for Bengals

It is a fairly significant step in the concussion protocol to get back on the field. It certainly doesn’t mean Chase will be able to get through the protocol in time for Sunday’s game, but it makes it far more likely than it seemed on Monday.

NFL News

Jerry Jones ‘extraordinarily disappointed’ after Cowboys loss to Buccaneers

This is exactly the result the Bengals need to avoid. Hopefully this prime time loss can serve as a warning to this team to not come out flat against a winless team on Sunday. Instead, come out and put it away early.

NFL Week 5 bold predictions: Jahmyr Gibbs breaks Barry Sanders’ record; ‘Hawks punish Brock Purdy

One is Marvin Harrison Jr. coming back to life against the Lions’ defense, which seems like an easy one to hammer home. The Lions are dealing with exactly what Cincinnati was last season. Every level of the defense is failing.

Ravens preparing two game plans with Lamar Jackson’s status vs. Falcons up in the air

It sounds like there is a very real possibility the Ravens are without Jackson, which would be a huge test for this new coaching staff. The team has traditionally struggled without him, which obviously is a huge hurdle for any team without their starting quarterback. It is an opportunity to show if things could be any different.

item.title: Mike Ditka, legendary NFL coach and tight end with the Bears, passes away at age-86
item.description: RIP Mike Ditka, 1939-2026.
item.content:encoded:
Legendary NFL head coach Mike Ditka passed away on Friday at age-86. His passing was first reported by Jarrett Payton, son of the best player Ditka ever coached, running back Walter Payton, and was later confirmed by multiple outlets.

Ditka became a legend by leading the 1985 Chicago Bears to one of the most dominant championship runs in league history. Led by Payton and arguably the best defense the NFL has ever seen, the Bears finished the regular season at 15-1, then outscored their three playoff opponents by a combined score of 96-10, capped by a blowout of the New England Patriots in Super Bowl XX.

The family shared this statement, via Jarrett Payton:

It is with profound sadness that we announce the passing of our beloved husband, father, grandfather, and friend, Mike Ditka. While the world knew Mike as a Hall of Fame football player, legendary coach, and leader of the Chicago Bears’ Super Bowl XX championship team, we knew him as the heart of our family. Mike will be missed beyond measure and remembered forever. With love and gratitude, The Ditka Family

Ditka was fired by the Bears in 1993. He’s still the only Super Bowl-winning coach in franchise history.

Ditka was also a Hall of Fame tight end during his playing days, and helped power the Bears to the 1963 NFL championship before the Super Bowl era. He was the NFL’s 1961 Offensive Rookie of the Year, and a two-time First-Team All-Pro. Ditka was also the New Orleans Saints’ head coach from 1997-1999.

Ditka’s Bears became a mainstream phenomenon on their way to the Super Bowl. The head coach’s sweater vest and mustache became an iconic look within pop culture. The Bears released “The Super Bowl Shuffle” song and music video nearly two months before they won Super Bowl XX. Ditka’s Bears never reached the heights of 1985 Super Bowl run again, but he did lead the team to seven playoff appearances in eight years before he was replaced by Dave Wannstedt.

The Bears play the rival Green Bay Packers on Sunday in Week 5. The Bears also played the Packers right after Payton passed away in 1999, and it was one of the most memorable games of the rivalry. Bill Swerski’s Super Fans became a popular Saturday Night Live skit depicting diehard Bears fans who ate sausages and worshipped Ditka.

We’ll update this story as it develops.

item.title: Mike Ditka, Hall of Famer and Chicago Bears legend, dies at 86
item.description: Mike Ditka, a three-time Super Bowl champion and two-time NFL Coach of the Year, died on Friday, Oct. 9, his family announced. He was 86.
item.content:encoded:
Mike Ditka, a three-time Super Bowl champion and two-time NFL Coach of the Year, died on Friday, Oct. 9, his family announced. He was 86.

Though best known as coach of the 1985 champion Chicago Bears, Ditka also revolutionized the tight end position after being drafted out of the University of Pittsburgh in 1961.

The news of Dikta's death was shared on social media by Jarrett Payton, son of Hall of Fame running back Walter Payton, who played for Ditka in Chicago.

"It is with profound sadness that we announce the passing of our beloved husband, father, grandfather, and friend, Mike Ditka," the family said in a statement shared by Payton. "While the world knew Mike as a Hall of Fame football player, legendary coach, and leader of the Chicago Bears’ Super Bowl XX championship team, we knew him as the heart of our family. Mike will be missed beyond measure and remembered forever."

It’s with a heavy heart that I’m sharing the Ditka family has announced the passing of Mike Ditka this morning.
Da Coach. Hall of Famer. The heartbeat of the ’85 Bears and a Super Bowl champion. Chicago won’t be the same.
Prayers to Diana and the family.
RIP, Coach. 🐻⬇️

Here’s… pic.twitter.com/NUDfwsjaNH

— Jarrett Payton (@paytonsun) October 9, 2026

Mike Ditka revolutionized the tight end position

Ditka added an offensive element to the tight end position that previously almost exclusively focused on blocking. In his first season, he caught 58 passes for 1,076 yards and 12 touchdowns en route to earning Rookie of the Year honors. Ditka became the first tight end in league history to surpass 1,000 yards; his 1,076 yards stood as the most receiving yards by a rookie tight end until Brock Bowers of the Las Vegas Raiders broke that mark in 2024.

Ditka was named to the Pro Bowl in his first five seasons and was an All-Pro in 1963, when the Bears won the NFL championship, and 1964.

He was traded to the Philadelphia Eagles in 1967, though his time there was limited by injuries. He played his final four seasons in Dallas, scoring a touchdown for the Cowboys in Super Bowl 6.

ON THIS DAY in 1972 — Dallas Cowboys defeated Miami Dolphins 24-3 at Tulane Stadium to win Super Bowl VI

The final touchdown of the game was a pass from Roger Staubach to his tight end ... Mike Ditka #DallasCowboyspic.twitter.com/BMx15DyrpK

— 𝗧𝗥𝗢𝗬 𝗛𝗨𝗚𝗛𝗘𝗦 (@TommySledge) January 16, 2020

Mike Ditka coaching career

He retired in 1973 and was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1988, becoming the first tight end admitted into Canton. 

Ditka became a special teams/wide receivers coach under the Cowboys' Tom Landry in 1973 and held the job for nine seasons, winning three NFC Championships and a Super Bowl.

"Iron Mike" then moved on to accept the Bears' head coaching job in 1982. Ditka led the 1985 Bears – considered one of the greatest NFL teams of all time – to victory in Super Bowl 20 after a 15-1 regular season.

He went 121-96 in 14 seasons between the Bears and New Orleans Saints, finishing his coaching career after the 1999 season. He was voted to the NFL's 75th and 100th Anniversary All-Time Teams and also was inducted into the College Football Hall of Fame in 1986.

Mike Ditka college

Born Oct. 18, 1939 in western Pennsylvania with the original surname "Dyczko" – his family changed it to "Ditka" for pronunciation ease – Ditka stayed home and played college football for the University of Pittsburgh Panthers.

As a coach, his gruff personality made him a Chicagoland hero, and his Bears sweaters became an iconic look. Ever the entertainer, Ditka also worked as a television analyst for CBS and ESPN during his post-coaching days. His appearance alongside Will Ferrell in the 2005 family comedy "Kicking & Screaming," in which he played himself, introduced him to a younger generation who came to appreciate him as "juice box boy" and provided a glimpse into his managerial style.

A symbol of toughness and always sporting a mustache in his coaching days, Ditka's style has influenced Halloween costumes for four decades now. But that all pales in comparison to his impact on the gridiron.

Contributing: Cale Clinton

item.title: Fantasy Football Rankings: Hayden Winks' WR Blueprint for Week 5
item.description: Fantasy football analyst Hayden Winks shares the Blueprint to the WR position for Week 5.
item.content:encoded:
The Blueprint is my weekly column and basically everything that I use to build out the most accurate rankings I can. There will be an RB column, this WR column on Thursdays and a combination column on the onesie positions. You will find film notes and endless charts. Maybe enough charts to stress test the Yahoo website. I kid.

It's impossible to get every ranking thoroughly early in the week, so be sure to keep checking in on these columns through Sunday morning. As always, my full rankings at every position are available.

1. Puka Nacua (vs. BUF) - 92.5 proj. receiving yards

Nacua's "pre-hernia" injury could be a serious long-term issue, but while he's in the lineup, he has the best projection every week. He got the best of an impressive Eagles secondary last week (WR5 on WR7 usage) while re-entering the lineup, and this matchup is far easier. The Rams have a monster 28.75-point team total (third) while hosting the Bills on Monday Night Football. Buffalo has allowed the third-most fantasy points to WRs this year, including a 2-TD game from Romeo Doubs (WR8) on top of big games from Amon-Ra St. Brown (WR4) and Nico Collins (WR9). They've missed CB1 Christian Benford recently, and the size issue from CB2 Maxwell Hairston will be one the Rams will certainly target here. They've allowed five TDs on just 27 man coverage reps this year.

2. Amon-Ra St. Brown (at ARI) - 79.5 proj. receiving yards

St. Brown is the WR5 on WR1 overall usage this season. His 11.5 targets per game keep him on pace for 196 targets this year. Dating back to last year, St. Brown has cleared 14.2 expected half PPR points in eight straight games with the Lions' secondary falling apart.

The Lions project for a league-high 30.0 points this week against a sorry Cardinals defense. They've allowed the fourth-most fantasy points to WRs so far, including top-17 finishes to Malik Nabers (WR10), Deebo Samuel (WR17), Jaxon Smith-Njigba (WR1) and Ladd McConkey (WR11). It's go time.

3. Jaxon Smith-Njigba (vs. SF) - 89.5 proj. receiving yards

JSN drafters on Yahoo have won 62% of their games, the highest of any WR through four weeks. He's the WR1 overall on WR3 overall usage, averaging a ridiculous 120 YPG on 10.3 targets.

Smith-Njigba faced the 49ers five times since 2024, scoring 7.8, 9.4, 11.4, 14.9, and 16.8 half PPR points in them. He's only scored a touchdown once in them while clearing 84 yards in 3 of 5. They've played him well all things considered, but their lack of pass rush right now works in JSN's favor. The Seahawks are at home with a 24.25-point team total (ninth). The 49ers gave up a score to Jaylen Waddle last week and Michael Wilson finished as the WR4 overall the week prior. It's a totally fine matchup for JSN.

4. CeeDee Lamb (vs. TB) - 79.5 proj. receiving yards

Lamb has 25 receiving first downs this year, only trailing 2011 Wes Welker for the most in NFL history through four weeks. He's shredded the Ravens and Texans defenses most recently, too. Lamb played a season-high 38% snaps in the slot to get away from CB1 Derek Stingley, including on his game-winning in-cut versus safety Jalen Pitre. It's a well-coached offense with quality protection and elite skill players. Dallas will compete for the scoring title. Lamb is the WR2 on WR4 usage so far, leading in receptions (9.3 per game) and yards (125 per game).

The blitz-heavy Bucs can catch bad OLs and QBs by surprise, but Prescott is amongst the best against the blitz over years of data. Lamb can be a quick outlet, as he was last week, but he can also get downfield where the Bucs have been exposed by Jordan Addison (WR10) and Denzel Boston (WR11) recently. Dallas has a 29.0-point team total (second).

5. Drake London (vs. BAL) - 89.5 proj. receiving yards

In 14 games with Michael Penix Jr. since 2024, London is now the WR3 (17.2 half PPR points) on WR8 usage (15.8 expected), WR1 overall target share (35%) and WR1 overall air yards (116 per game). He's finished as the WR2 overall and the WR24 overall (without a TD) in his two games with him this year. Penix has executed his under-center play action reps and is moving just enough to have a productive season. Penix wants to drive the ball, and London is running more deep breaking routes in this offense to fit in. There will be some underneath work, but London could be a killer on intermediate throws. Penix had an awesome anticipation throw before a zone defender had time to make a play on the ball on a corner route last night. London has an obvious case to be an early Round 2 pick if drafting today.

The Ravens have a good defense, but they are still working out the kinks and don't have an overpowering pass-rushing unit in general. They've allowed the eighth-most fantasy points to WRs so far, including a career-high 145 yards to Carnell Tate last week. CeeDee Lamb (WR13) and Chris Olave (WR9) had their usual games against them as clear-cut top targets. Atlanta has a 23.25-point team total (12th) at home.

6. Nico Collins (at TEN) - 79.5 proj. receiving yards

Collins is the WR3 on WR5 usage this season, averaging 9.0 targets per game as one of the most dominant players on tape. There is no competition for targets in Houston with its run game in shambles once again; it'd make sense to start leaning into the pass game more than ever. CJ Stroud is playing well.

The matchup is also a solid one. Houston has a 23.0-point team total (13th) in Tennessee, and its defense is far more dominant at DT than anywhere else right now. Teams should be comfortable passing against them in neutral situations. I've seen DeVonta Smith (WR6), Dontayvion Wicks (WR27) and Zay Flowers (WR6) give them major trouble this year. CB1 Alontae Taylor and CB2 Cor'Dale Flott are players to target as mismatches for Collins' size and speed. He has 79+ yards or a TD in all five career games against the Titans, including a WR4 overall finish in Week 11 last season.

7. Michael Wilson (vs. DET) - 72.5 proj. receiving yards

Wilson has some of the best WR tape of 2026. He's a great route runner at the top of his break, he's physical and he has moments at the catch point. His third-and-1 deep out route last week was sensational stuff. Down six points with seconds remaining at the 5-yard line, Wilson was targeted on first-, second- and fourth-down. Were they completed? No, but that's a great sign that he's trusted down there.

Through four weeks, Wilson is the WR22 on WR6 usage. Since Week 11 of last year, Wilson only trails Puka Nacua, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Chris Olave and Amon-Ra St. Brown in fantasy points per game (15.5). He's WR2 in air yards per game and WR3 in targets per game during that stretch, too. I think he's far more of a fantasy WR2 than the market believes.

The matchup is the best one in the NFL. WR rooms facing the Lions are averaging 56 more yards per game against them compared to the rest of their schedule right now, easily the most in the NFL. They desperately miss S Brian Branch (Achilles) and other starting CBs, and they're put in tough spots because the Lions offense is scoring at will. Just look at Tetairoa McMillan (WR1 overall), Garrett Wilson (WR3) and Chris Olave (WR6 without a TD) versus the Lions. The Cardinals project for 24.5 points at home, while the Lions have a league-leading 30.0 total. Get excited.

8. Davante Adams (vs. BUF) - 62.5 proj. receiving yards

Adams is the WR16 on WR6 usage in 18 games with Puka Nacua since last year. He busted last week after multiple fingertip missed plays for explosives and touchdowns, but the underlying numbers were otherwise there with WR10 expected points (15.6) and nine targets. Nacua is a baller still but also maybe a step slower while playing with this "pre-hernia" injury, and Adams is moving quite well on tape right now.

The matchup with the Bills is tasty. It's at home with extra rest on Monday Night Football, and they've been shredded by physical WRs this year, especially without CB1 Christian Benford. Romeo Doubs (WR8) and Efton Chism III had SportsCenter moments last week, while Amon-Ra St. Brown (WR4) and Nico Collins (WR9) did their thing in previous outings. A 28.75-point team total (third) is the final obvious tell to start Adams as an upside WR1/2.

9. Justin Jefferson (at NO)

Jefferson (ankle) expects to play after missing last week with a low-ankle sprain, even with the Vikings having a bye next week. They'd only let him play if he was truly ready to go given that context. I'm not docking him for injury. Jordan Addison is also dealing with a hamstring injury, though he was back at practice Thursday.

10. Chris Olave (vs. MIN) - 79.5 proj. receiving yards

Olave has a seven-game streak of 15+ half PPR points and 14+ expected half PPR points. He's the WR6 overall on WR2 usage this year with Tyler Shough comfortably leading the NFL in dropbacks. He'd be an early Round 2 pick if redrafting today.

The Vikings will easily be the toughest test yet, especially with LT Kelvin Banks Jr. (IR) being replaced by an inexperienced player who is allowing a near league-high rate of pressures. That gets turned up against DC Brian Flores, who is as good as anyone in league history at destroying protection rules. They also play with two deep safeties often, so it's a bit harder to find the explosive plays that have made Olave one of the best fantasy WRs in the game. Minnesota has allowed the 19th-most fantasy points to WRs, largely driven by a massive downfield outing from Christian Watson (WR2) in Week 1. They haven't allowed a top-30 fantasy WR since then versus the Dolphins, Bucs and Bears. The Saints project for 19.5 points (22nd), far fewer than normal.

11. Garrett Wilson (vs. CLE) - 69.5 proj. receiving yards

Wilson was rug-pulled by a Jets outing that resulted in the fourth-fewest plays (32) in a single game in NFL history. The Bears also did a good job of limiting Wilson on their dropbacks, but that will go down as an outlier game. Wilson was the WR15 on WR25 usage and the WR3 on WR9 usage in the previous two outings with Breece Hall (quad), AD Mitchell (finger) and Mason Taylor (thumb) all sidelined. They're all still injured, so Wilson's ceiling is far higher than usual.

The Browns are the only team in the NFL actually playing man coverage at a notable rate. They've used it 88 times. The next closest is at 57, by the Patriots. They can do it because CB1 Denzel Ward is having another great season, and they are enjoying a great season from S Ronnie Hickman. This will be a "ball up top" matchup. The Jets are projected for 21.0 points (21st) while at home.

12. George Pickens (vs. TB) - 69.5 proj. receiving yards

Pickens is the most obvious buy-low ever. He's only the WR39 on WR23 usage this season, but the tape is showing plenty of DPIs called on him and some bad luck. There will be huge games coming with the Cowboys already leading the NFL in points per drive (3.4) without star LG Tyler Smith, who returns for Thursday Night Football. Dating back to last year, Pickens is the WR17 on WR12 usage with 22% of the targets in games with CeeDee Lamb.

The Cowboys are projected for the second-most points at home against an 0-4 Bucs team. This historically is a pass-funnel defense, and the Todd Bowles blitzes aren't going to catch Dak Prescott by surprise as much as they've worked against lesser offenses. Splash plays from Jordan Addison (WR10) and Denzel Boston (WR11) are reasons for upside WR2 faith. We can panic if Pickens doesn't come through tonight ...

13. Christian Watson (vs. CHI) - 59.5 proj. receiving yards

Watson had his worst game of the year last week, but nothing has materially changed other than Tucker Kraft is becoming more involved after a horrible start to his season coming off a torn ACL. That could hurt Watson at the margins, especially when (if) Josh Jacobs returns. Watson is still the WR8 on WR12 usage and WR14 targets per game (7.8).

A matchup with the Bears may be a little more difficult than it seemed pre-season after DC Dennis Allen has gotten the most of his injured defense, but it's still a fun game to target. Jalen Coker had a WR1 overall finish against them in Week 1, for crying out loud. The Packers are projected for 22.0 points (16th) as slight home dogs. Watson had three games against the Bears last year; 36 yards with a score in the playoff loss, a 17-yard dud in Week 16 and a WR5 overall finish in Week 14.

14. Matthew Golden (vs. CHI) - 59.5 proj. receiving yards

Golden is the WR17 on WR10 usage and WR9 targets per game (9.0) this season, with 10+ half PPR points and 10+ expected half PPR points in 3-of-4 contests. He's been a more explosive version of the Romeo Doubs role from last year, but now there's not a No. 3 receiver to get "gimme" looks. Those can trickle down to Golden, too.

See more about the matchup in the Christian Watson blurb from above, noting the primary difference is Golden's matchup with CB2 Tyrique Stevenson is far better than against CB1 Jaylon Johnson.

15. Zay Flowers (at ATL) - 69.5 proj. receiving yards

Flowers is not expected to have Lamar Jackson this time around, which obviously impacts his efficiency a ton, but OC Declan Doyle is very reliant on Flowers being the focal point of the pass game. He's being used underneath in ways that should keep his floor high with Tyler Huntley at QB. His yards per route being in his own stratosphere is helpful when readjusting for his new situation. He's the WR6 on WR15 usage, including two half-games.

The matchup is a strong one, too. The Falcons are well coached but down CB1 A.J. Terrell and two impact pass rushers. They've allowed the fourth-most passing yards per game (277) and seventh-most fantasy points to WRs so far. Chris Olave (116 yards), Christian Watson (96 yards) and Tetairoa McMillan (101 yards) all have been excellent as the top targets in their offenses against them recently. Baltimore's 20.25-point team total is just about seven points less than normal, and Derrick Henry's has a disproportionate touchdown share in this offense.

16. Malik Nabers (at WAS) - 59.5 proj. receiving yards

Update: Nabers (knee) had soreness on Wednesday and missed practice, but returned on Thursday.

Hand up — I got this one way wrong last week when I ranked him closer to the WR3 range. Nabers was the WR10 on WR30 usage with multiple explosives. He beat a heavy-footed LB on a seam ball for a TD, high-pointed a lollipop from Jameis Winston on a deep corner route and had a great circus route with massive separation. There was some underneath success, too, including a hitch route that led to two broken tackles. We're inching closer to 90% health as we head into October, and with the Giants at 3-1, it'll likely be Jameis for the near future. Nabers is trending upwards as the WR33 on WR38 usage this season.

The matchup is a great one. The Commanders are doing the chaos at the line of scrimmage thing a lot more than others with new DC Daronte Jones (from the Brian Flores tree), and it's funneled a lot more yards via the air (eighth-most) than on the ground (27th). Star WRs have had big outings against them already; JSN (WR1 overall) and CeeDee Lamb (WR3 overall). There's no reason to believe in Mike Sainristill in boundary coverage right now. The Giants project for 19.0 points (26th), however and it will almost always be a fairly run-heavy plan under Harbaugh.

17. Parker Washington (vs. PHI) - 59.5 proj. receiving yards

18. Jaylen Waddle (at LAC) - 59.5 proj. receiving yards

Waddle's season-long ceiling isn't hitting as we'd hoped. His 21% target share and WR37 expected half PPR points sit too far down to be trusted as more than an inconsistent WR2/3 in fantasy. Bo Nix's quick trigger to the checkdown has left some potential intermediate and downfield throws on the field, and the Sean Payton offense will always have schemed up targets to others. Waddle did have two screen receptions in Week 4, and his overall involvement could tick up with valued WR3 Pat Bryant (IR, ankle) now injured. Waddle has also dropped a couple of passes for potential explosives this year to tilt us further. He's the WR32 per game. I'm waiting for the 50-yard YAC moment ...

19. Jameson Williams (at ARI) - 49.5 proj. receiving yards

Dud-dud-dud-boom. That's the story with Jamo. He had three comeback receptions, one screen, one quick out and one go ball Cover 3 hole shot heading into halftime in a wild loss to the Panthers. His day could've been bigger had he come down with two designed chunk plays (double move down the sideline and bootleg play-action dig). Williams ultimately finished WR19 on WR20 usage without scoring a touchdown, and the fact that the Lions defense yet again couldn't get stops bodes well for Williams' WR3 odds this year. He's been the WR45 on WR33 usage this season as a positive regression candidate.

20. DK Metcalf (vs. IND) - 49.5 proj. receiving yards

21. Josh Downs (at PIT) - 59.5 proj. receiving yards

22. Mike Evans (at SEA) - 49.5 proj. receiving yards

23. Romeo Doubs (vs. LV) - 49.5 proj. receiving yards

Doubs has been the wildest rollercoaster of the year, but Week 4 was nothing but a total smash. Aside from an extremely low ball that was tossed by Doubs into the air for an INT, Doubs played well. He had a skinny post TD, a 4th-and-3 slant win and a one-handed fade TD. His WR8 finish was on WR11 expected half PPR points, and the Patriots also lost Mack Hollins (calf) around halftime. They're running out of bodies for Drake Maye to throw to, so Doubs' value is absolutely trending up. His expected half PPR points have climbed every week: 2.6, 5.2, 6.7, 15.4.

24. DJ Moore (at LAR)

25. Luther Burden III (at GB) - 49.5 proj. receiving yards

26. Rome Odunze (at GB) - 39.5 proj. receiving yards

27. Carnell Tate (vs. HOU) - 49.5 proj. receiving yards

Tate had a career-high 15.8 expected half PPR points in Week 4 and his usage has climbed in three straight games. Results were mixed, but things are generally trending up. Cam Ward delivered a couple of wow throws out of structure to Tate, who was only targeted five+ yards downfield on all 12 of his looks. There were some high throws with offbeat timing in there, but the volume is real and there will be go-ball explosives eventually. He had a double-move penalty drawn on him from All-Pro S Kyle Hamilton as an example. Tate is the WR34 on WR22 usage to start his career, and I don't see Calvin Ridley, Wan'Dale Robinson and others eating into his alpha status.

28. Dohnte Meyers (at MIA)

This assumes Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) are out. More later.

29. Stefon Diggs (vs. NYG)

Diggs (hamstring) did not practice on Wednesday. More later.

30. Devaughn Vele (vs. MIN) - 39.5 proj. receiving yards

Vele is a real fantasy WR3. He became a full-time player in Week 12 last year, and he's the WR22 on WR17 usage in eight games since. This year, Vele is the WR21 on WR13 usage with Tyler Shough leading the NFL with 48 dropbacks per game. Only six other teams are above 40 for reference.

Vele's extreme catch radius comes in handy, as we saw with his toe-tapping garbage-time touchdown on Monday Night Football. He also has a goal-line fade as the lone WR on the field this season, and he's consistently targeted on breaking routes about 10 yards down the field. With Jordyn Tyson realistically targeting a Week 9 return, Vele is looking like a high-end rental.

31. Denzel Boston (at NYJ) - 49.5 proj. receiving yards

32. Ladd McConkey (vs. DEN)

McConkey (foot) did not practice on Wednesday.

33. Malik Washington (vs. CIN) - 39.5 proj. receiving yards

34. Deebo Samuel Sr. (at SEA) - 39.5 proj. receiving yards

35. Jordan Addison (at NO)

Update: Addison (hamstring) was back at practice on Thursday, and Justin Jefferson (ankle) plans to play.

Addison is the WR24 on WR36 usage over the past two weeks without Justin Jefferson (ankle), and it might be another outing as the alpha with the Vikings on bye in Week 6. Addison can be occasionally bullied out of his route, but there are enough downfield moments with the sprinkling of a screen to be trusted in fantasy lineups for the time being. Kyler Murray hasn't had too many anticipatory throws over the middle beyond quick seam balls, but they are using Addison on them whenever Kyler wants to deliver it. They did have a great corner route, so the rapport isn't non-existent. The bigger issue is the Vikings are 29th in neutral pass rate with a 9.1% sack rate (fifth-worst).

36. Marvin Harrison Jr. (vs. DET) - 39.5 proj. receiving yards

Marv had a productive Week 4 for the Cardinals, even if the box score was underwhelming again. He had a great ball-tracking fade TD early on, but he also drew two DPIs in and around the end zone on designed looks for him. The Cardinals also had him as the lone receiver at the goal line for a quick slant that was, of course, completely shut down. Harrison is going to be significantly better than this WR88 on WR84 usage start, and I've noticed more buy-in from him in recent weeks. If there's a week to buy low, it's against the Lions at home with a wild game total. That'd be especially true if Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is banged up.

37. KC Concepcion (at NYJ) - 39.5 proj. receiving yards

38. Keon Coleman (at LAR) - 49.5 proj. receiving yards

39. Tre Tucker (at NE) - 39.5 proj. receiving yards

40. Emeka Egbuka (at DAL) - 39.5 proj. receiving yards

Jalon Daniels was just fine in his debut as an undrafted free agent. That was the earliest into a rookie season that an UDFA QB has started a game. The Bucs tried to hide him with a season-low neutral pass rate, and Daniels is going to scramble around a bit, too. That said, Daniels has a live arm and is willing to sling it. There could be garbage-time production here. He's good enough for that.

Egbuka was only targeted three times last week, leading to a WR83 finish on WR66 usage. Playing him in fantasy is absolutely daring, as the Bucs made sure to get Chris Godwin Jr. and Cade Otton involved underneath more often. Egbuka is going to work downfield more than them, making it harder to find a floor. Egbuka hasn't been overly impressive on tape either, even if the offense is doing more creative things with him before and at the snap.

The Cowboys have the worst-graded zone defense this year, per PFF, if you're feeling risky or are just desperate. They've allowed the 10th-most fantasy points to WRs this year, most recently getting smoked by Nico Collins (WR3), Zay Flowers (104 yards on a couple dozen routes) and Stefon Diggs (WR8). The Cowboys will have new CB1 Joey Porter Jr. available for more snaps this week, and he'll very likely see Egbuka the most with Godwin hid in the slot more often. It's too much for me to bank on. The Bucs project for 19.5 points on the road.

item.title: Fantasy Football Start/Sit Advice: Omarion Hampton, Brock Purdy, more players in Week 5
item.description: Scott Pianowski plays traffic cop with some tough fantasy football calls for Week 5.
item.content:encoded:
Start-sit decisions can be vexing for even the best of fantasy managers. If you need help setting your fantasy football lineups, Scott Pianowski offers some assistance with his Week 5 traffic report.

Green Light ✅

QB Jacoby Brissett vs. Lions: Detroit’s back seven has been shredded by everybody, and Josh Allen is the only no-doubt star it’s faced. Brissett’s 2026 season has been inconsistent, but he has help (Trey McBride, Michael Wilson) and should race past 40 pass attempts. First team to 30 points wins.

TE Isaiah Likely at Commanders: He’s, at worst, the second read in this passing game, and Likely quietly has the highest target share of all tight ends. Jameis Winston played buttoned-up football in Week 3 but was back to YOLO Winston in Week 4 — that’s a positive trend for fantasy managers. Washington's defense presents a plus-matchup as well.

TE Mike Gesicki at Dolphins: It’s a revenge game for Gesicki, who spent five years in South Florida. Joe Burrow likes Gesicki in the red area (three touchdowns), and Gesicki might see extra work if Cincinnati is missing either of its star wideouts. Miami’s pass defense has been surprisingly competent on the flanks but exploitable down the seam.

RB Aaron Jones Sr. at Saints: The Minnesota passing game is a mess right now, with Kyler Murray struggling to get his mojo back. That might not matter in Week 5, as Jones can lug the mail. The estimable veteran is averaging 23 touches per week over his last three starts, and the New Orleans front seven has been gashed on the ground (nine rushing touchdowns, 147.8 yards per week).

Yellow Light 😕

RB Quinshon Judkins at Jets: We can’t give Judkins green-light status while he’s still chugging along at 3.0 yards per carry. But his touch count has risen every week, largely because the Browns are using him more in the passing game (15 catches this year, just 26 his rookie season). Cleveland overhauled its entire offensive line before the year, so let’s give it some time to jell. Game script shouldn’t be a problem at the Jets.

RB Will Shipley vs. Jaguars (London): Shipley was a reasonable waiver wire target, given the injures in the Philly running back room. But the Philadelphia offensive line has fallen apart, and the Jaguars present a daunting matchup (allowing just 3.3 YPC). Shipley should easily get double-digit opportunities, but be reasonable with expectations.

RB TreVeyon Henderson vs. Raiders: He’s stuck on just one reception — after catching 35 passes last year — and he’s seldom the guy tabbed at the goal line. But Rhamondre Stevenson is dinged up and the Raiders have been leaky against the run all year (5.2 YPC, 134.5 yards per game). This is a week where Henderson can be a proactive flex play.

WR Josh Downs at Steelers: I’m torn on Downs, a nice player who still might be working with a capped ceiling. As a smaller receiver (5-foot-9, 171 pounds), he’s unlikely to see a lot of red-zone work; he’s been targeted just once inside the 15-yard line. It was also frustrating to see Downs do little against a leaky Washington secondary last week. The Steelers defense could also challenge Downs — it’s been better in slot coverage than it has been on the outside. Downs remains in the WR3 bucket: playable, but not a slam dunk.

Red Light 🚨

QB Brock Purdy at Seahawks: I’m gladly on the Purdy bandwagon almost every week, but the Seattle defense has proven his Kryptonite. Purdy faced the Seahawks twice last January (once in the playoffs) and it was a nightmare: just nine total points, zero touchdowns, a piddly 267 passing yards. The Seattle defense is once again shredding (a scant 5.2 YPA allowed, just 144.8 yards per game), so this might be the one time you bench Purdy.

RB Alvin Kamara vs. Vikings: He’s capable of scoring fantasy points even if he’s not efficient — that’s how Kamara escaped Monday, bailed out by touchdown deodorant. And Kendre Miller (Week 4 fumble) seems to be in the doghouse. But the top-ranked Minnesota defense might force the Saints to prematurely junk the running game. I’m not interested in threading the Kamara needle in Week 5.

RB Omarion Hampton vs. Broncos: The Chargers can’t worry about draft capital and contracts and such right now, they just have to identify their best players and rely on them. And it’s inescapable that Keaton Mitchell has been at least as good as Hampton the last couple of weeks. No matter who the Chargers rely on in the backfield, the offensive line is once again an injury-ravaged mess. Facing an absurdly-difficult schedule, the Chargers have crash-landing potential in 2026.

WR Malik Washington vs. Bengals: He’s the target hog in Miami, if that matters to you — 17 catches for 219 yards, enough to earn rostership in most leagues. But the Dolphins are averaging just 25 pass attempts per week and only have one touchdown pass through the opening quarter. Washington himself might have an end-zone allergy, stuck on three spikes for his 89 career receptions.
